No new manufacturer quotation, default from engine size/code, new enum, octane field, alternate-fuel capability or other-year/market/engine approval is inferred. Gasoline classification does not relax the manufacturer premium-fuel requirement.

assertions.source_context: Human-adjudicated conclusion by project_owner: The production 392 specification explicitly describes a conventional alternator/12V battery electrical system, joined to ESG through the US guide. This supports nonhybrid, but the enum is a derived conclusion rather than a direct manufacturer declaration.

Human-adjudicated conclusion by project_owner: US ESG/27X guide and production-MY2021 manufacturer release/specification establish the 6.4L production engine; a contemporary production technical report explicitly describes natural aspiration. Proposed classification remains derived because retained manufacturer production material does not explicitly assert induction.

Human-adjudicated conclusion by project_owner: The project owner approves gasoline for this exact production MY2021 US Rubicon 392. The manufacturer specifies Premium 91 octane (R+M)/2 — required for its documented 6.4L engine. In this engine-specific fuel requirement, premium octane is a gasoline grade, not a separate broad fuel category. Under accepted RA-044 the existing fuel_type value is gasoline; octane grade is outside the five-field powertrain identity. This is a supported human-adjudicated classification, not a claim that the retained specification literally states the gasoline enum.
